key_themes: US-Iran peace deal signals push oil to ~$86, easing inflation fears and fueling broad equity rally
SpaceX prices record-breaking $75B IPO at $135/share, valued at ~$1.75 trillion
Chipmaker rebound: MU +12%, SNDK +14%, INTC +10% after prior-week semiconductor selloff
Oracle tumbles ~12% on $95B AI capex guidance and $40B debt/equity raise plan despite earnings beat
After-hours earnings catalyst: Adobe, Lennar, RH all reporting today

stocks.discussion_driver: SpaceX priced its record-breaking $75B IPO at $135/share on June 11, valuing the company at $1.77 trillion — the largest IPO in history. The company merged with xAI prior to listing, adding AI infrastructure exposure alongside its Starlink and launch businesses. Trading begins on Nasdaq under SPCX on June 12.
bull_case: Starlink generates $8B+ in recurring annual revenue with 7M+ subscribers and near-monopoly on commercial launch services, providing a durable cash flow base
xAI merger and Falcon 9/Heavy reusability create a vertically integrated aerospace/AI powerhouse; ARK Invest projects $3.1T valuation by 2030
bear_case: Morningstar pegs fair value near $780B vs $1.77T IPO valuation, implying 55%+ downside if the AI/space premium compresses
Key-person risk from Elon Musk's attention spread across Tesla, xAI, and SpaceX; government contract concentration adds political risk

stocks.discussion_driver: Oracle tumbled ~12% on June 11 despite a Q4 FY2026 earnings beat (EPS $2.11 vs $1.89 est.), as investors were rattled by $95B FY2027 AI capex guidance and plans to raise $40B via new debt and equity. Cloud infrastructure revenue surged 93% YoY to $5.8B, but remaining performance obligations and capital allocation concerns overshadowed the beat. The selloff creates a potential re-entry point with 39% average analyst upside.
bull_case: Cloud infrastructure revenue surged 93% YoY to $5.8B and remaining performance obligations grew 363% to $638B, providing exceptional multi-year revenue visibility
Post-earnings selloff at $183 creates a potential entry point — 35 analysts rate ORCL Buy with an average target of $255, representing 39% upside from current levels
bear_case: $95B FY2027 capex guidance and $40B debt/equity raise plan raise concerns about balance sheet leverage, EPS dilution, and management's ability to deploy capital efficiently
Stock remains 47% below its 52-week high of $345.72 — the market has persistently struggled to sustain a premium valuation on Oracle

stocks.discussion_driver: Micron surged ~12% on June 11 as part of a broad semiconductor sector rebound driven by Iran peace deal optimism, recovering from a 15%+ correction off its June 3 all-time high of $1,089.29. The SOXX chipmaker gauge jumped nearly 8% on the day. Micron leads the AI HBM supercycle trade and is up 179% YTD, though most analyst price targets have yet to catch up with the rapid rally.
bull_case: AI data center demand is driving record HBM orders at premium pricing; analysts describe the AI memory trade as still in 'mid-innings' with significant runway remaining
Forward P/E of ~9.8x is dramatically below the Nasdaq composite's ~26x forward multiple, suggesting meaningful valuation upside relative to growth if the cycle sustains
bear_case: Stock up 179% YTD has outpaced most analyst price targets — consensus sits at $737.63, roughly 20% below current price, indicating the rally may be overextended near-term
Memory semiconductor cycles are historically volatile; any demand slowdown, inventory build, or HBM pricing normalization could trigger a sharp correction from elevated levels

stocks.discussion_driver: SanDisk surged ~14% on June 11, hitting a new all-time intraday high of $1,918.99, powered by the broad semiconductor rebound and extraordinary fundamental momentum. The company is up 552% YTD as one of the 'Parabolic 7' memory/AI stocks. Q3 FY2026 revenue grew 251% YoY to $5.95B and Q4 guidance calls for $7.75-8.25B in revenue at $30-$33 non-GAAP EPS, driving a string of major analyst target upgrades.
bull_case: Explosive fundamentals: Q3 revenue up 251% YoY with Q4 guidance implying $30-$33 EPS; BofA raised target to $2,100 and Cantor Fitzgerald has a $2,900 target implying 52%+ upside
AI data center NAND flash and HBM demand appears structural, not cyclical; forward PE of ~11.7x suggests earnings are rapidly growing into an elevated stock price
bear_case: Trailing PE of 59.24x and stock at all-time highs after a 552% YTD gain creates extreme mean-reversion risk if any guidance miss or memory cycle turn occurs
Average analyst consensus target of $1,843 is below the current $1,902 price, indicating many analysts haven't kept pace with the rally and potential overextension risk

stocks.discussion_driver: Intel jumped ~10% on June 11 following a Loop Capital upgrade from Hold to Buy (target $75), amplified by broad semiconductor sector tailwinds from Iran deal optimism. Bank of America also double-upgraded Intel to Buy and raised its target from $96 to $135, marking a major shift in analyst sentiment around Intel's turnaround story. Despite the surge, the consensus from 48 analysts remains a Hold with an average target of $92.17 — below current price — reflecting valuation skepticism.
bull_case: Bank of America double-upgraded to Buy with a $135 price target, and Loop Capital upgraded to Buy, marking a meaningful shift in analyst sentiment around Intel's turnaround under new leadership
Semiconductor sector tailwinds from Iran deal-driven optimism and AI infrastructure spending boom; stock remains 21% below its 52-week high with further recovery potential
bear_case: Forward PE of 98.32x is 185% above the semiconductor industry median of 34.45x — an extremely rich valuation given ongoing competitiveness challenges vs AMD and Nvidia
Consensus from 48 analysts is Hold with an average target of $92.17 — 12% below current price — suggesting most analysts view the stock as overvalued after the recent surge
